note: Non-urn `grantId` — HCP grant identifiers are urn:uuid.
Missing `revokedAt` — the grant-revoked event carries when the revocation took effect.
`revokedAt` as Unix seconds — instants are RFC 3339 strings, even though the SET's own `iat` is numeric.
A SET `events` wrapper in the payload — the Type URI replaces it.
`reason` outside the enumeration — the delegation's own reason for ending (HCP 17.6) is never sent; only `revoked` or `delegation-ended`.
`reason` in another casing — `delegation-ended` is HCP's value (HCP 8.2, 17.6) and is carried verbatim.
A `delegation-ended` notice without `revokedAt` — it carries the instant the delegation ended.
Missing `grantId` — the notice names the grant that ended.
Missing `noticeId` — every notice carries the SET's `jti`, the same on every delivery attempt, so the client can deduplicate (HCP 9.9).
Non-urn `noticeId` — the SET's `jti` is carried as a urn:uuid, the form HCP 9.9's own `jti` and every other HCP identifier take.
A member in the acknowledgement — RFC 8935's 202 Accepted has no body, so the payload is the empty object.
